meta.title: CIS-DF Practice Quiz
meta.subtitle: ServiceNow Certified Implementation Specialist – Data Foundations (CMDB & CSDM)

questions.text:
A CMDB Architect intends to build a CMDB using CSDM guidance.

Which CMDB tables will the architect use to build the CSDM sell/consume domain?

options.t: Business Capability, Information Object, Business Application
Application Service, Technology Management Service (Technical Service), Technology Management Offering (Technical Service Offering)

questions.explanation: The Sell/Consume domain is the layer end users and business consumers actually interact with. Business Service is what the business offers, and Business Service Offering is the specific version/tier of it (e.g., "Gold" vs "Standard" support). Business Capability and Information Object belong to the Design domain, while Application Service and Technology Service belong to the Manage Technical Services domain.
questions.analogy: Think of a restaurant menu: the Business Service is "Dinner Service," and Business Service Offerings are the specific menu tiers customers pick from ("Prix Fixe" vs "À la Carte"). The kitchen equipment behind the scenes (Application/Technology Services) isn't what the customer orders from.

questions.text: Drag and drop the application service type to the best description. (Only the following pairs were legible in the source screenshot; the remaining item positions were cut off.)

pairs.desc: Recommended for mission-critical applications that require a precise approach using patterns
Best fit to map cloud-native, container-based, or virtual machine environments

questions.explanation: Service Mapping offers different discovery approaches depending on how precise you need the map to be. Connection Suggestion (pattern-based) traces real network connections between processes, so it's used where accuracy really matters (mission-critical apps). Top-down mapping starts from an entry point and is well suited to dynamic, cloud-native or containerized environments where the underlying infrastructure changes constantly.
questions.analogy: Connection Suggestion is like tracing every wire behind your TV to know exactly what's plugged into what — precise but effort-intensive, worth it for the systems that really matter. Top-down mapping is more like glancing at the whole entertainment center and guessing the setup from what's visible — faster, and well suited to setups that get rearranged often (like cloud/container workloads).

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator would like to minimize stale CIs in the CMDB.

Which CMDB Health Dashboard scorecard displays this information?
questions.explanation: The Correctness KPI on the CMDB Health Dashboard checks whether CMDB data is accurate and current — it covers duplicates, orphan CIs, and staleness (CIs not updated within a defined time frame, 60 days by default). Completeness checks whether required/recommended fields are populated, and Compliance checks CIs against desired-state audits.
questions.analogy: Completeness asks "did you fill out the whole form?" Compliance asks "does the form match the rules?" Correctness asks "is this form still up to date, or has it gone stale in the drawer?" Staleness is squarely a Correctness concern.

questions.text:
A CMDB Data Owner has requested better insights on the different data sources that make up the CMDB data set. The Platform Owner knows that the new Service Graph Connector Central plugin is just what is needed.

After installing the plugin, what workspace will have the new Service Graph Connector Central tab available?
questions.explanation: The CMDB Workspace is ServiceNow's central hub for everything CMDB-related — data quality, data sources, duplicates, and connector management all live there so admins don't have to hop between separate apps. Service Graph Connector Central surfaces as a tab inside this same workspace.
questions.analogy: Think of the CMDB Workspace as mission control, and Service Graph Connector Central as one more screen on the same control panel — you don't need to walk into a different room to check it.

questions.text:
A Configuration Manager needs to enable a CMDB Data Manager policy to remove records from a CI Class while retaining the ability to restore them within a specified period.

Which policy type should the Configuration Manager create?
questions.explanation: An Archive policy moves CI records out of the active CMDB tables into archive tables, but keeps them retrievable for a retention period — useful for compliance or historical reference. Delete permanently removes records (no restore), Retire just marks a CI as no longer in use (it stays in the live table), and Certification is about verifying data accuracy, not removing records.
questions.analogy: Archiving is like moving old files into a labeled storage box in the attic — out of your daily workspace, but you can still go get the box back if you need it. Deleting is shredding the paper.

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator is asked to clean up the CMDB duplicates.

What is the preferred way to manage this task?

options.t: My Tasks in the Application Navigator
The de-duplication dashboard on the CMDB workspace

questions.explanation: The de-duplication dashboard in CMDB Workspace is purpose-built to surface duplicate CIs (identified via CI Identification Rules) and provide tools like the Duplicate CI Remediator to merge or resolve them in bulk, rather than hunting through generic task lists.
questions.analogy: It's the difference between sorting your inbox manually versus using a dedicated "find duplicate emails" tool that shows you all the copies at once and lets you merge them in a few clicks.

questions.text:
A Business Relationship Manager in an organization wants to implement Service Portfolio Management (SPM) and to present offerings to business consumers.

Which CSDM Domain does this align with?
questions.explanation: Presenting offerings to business consumers and managing a service portfolio (what's sold/offered to the business) is exactly what the Sell/Consume domain represents — it holds Business Service, Business Service Offering, and Service Portfolio-related tables used by SPM.
questions.analogy: This is the "storefront" layer — the catalog page customers browse and subscribe to, as opposed to the kitchen (Build) or the equipment running behind the counter (Service Delivery).

questions.text:
A Service Owner needs to view related items, such as Active Incidents and Planned Changes, directly on the home node of the Unified Map.

Which work area would allow the Service Owner to meet this goal?
questions.explanation: The contextual side panel in the Unified Map shows detail and related records — like open incidents or planned changes — for whichever node you've selected, without leaving the map view.
questions.analogy: It's like clicking a pin on a map app and having a small info card slide out with reviews, hours, and directions for that exact location — you get the detail without losing your place on the map.

questions.text: Which are CMDB Data Manager end of life policy types? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation: CMDB Data Manager's core end-of-life policy types are Retire, Archive, Delete, Attestation, and Certification. "Lost," "Decommission," and "Disposed" are lifecycle status values you might see elsewhere, but they aren't Data Manager policy types.
questions.analogy: Retire and Archive are two named tools in the same toolbox — "Decommission" or "Lost" describe the state a CI ends up in, not the tool you used to get it there.

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator wants to leverage the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard.

What are benefits of using this application? (Choose 2)

options.t: Has a framework to create custom metrics for the CMDB
Checks that important data is valid and properly configured
Provides playbooks to assist in the remediation of potential risks
Uses automation to remediate potential risks

questions.explanation: The CMDB and CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard (a free store app) checks that key data — like identification rules, principal classes, and locations — is valid and properly configured, and it can trigger automation to fix certain issues it finds. It links out to remediation playbooks for guidance, but the playbooks themselves are reference material, not a separate "framework for custom metrics."
questions.analogy: Picture a car's dashboard warning light system: it checks your engine is configured correctly (B), and in some cases can auto-adjust settings (D) — while the owner's manual (the playbook) explains what to do next, but isn't a metric-building framework itself.

questions.text:
A CMDB Configuration Manager intends to implement CMDB Data Manager delete and archive policies for all server records in the New York datacenter.

In which lifecycle state would servers be affected by these new policies?
questions.explanation: Delete and Archive policies are end-of-life actions that follow retirement — a CI is normally retired first, and only once it's in the End of Life - Retired state does it become a candidate for archiving or deletion. You generally wouldn't delete/archive a CI that's still in active use.
questions.analogy: It's a sequence, not a shortcut: an item gets "discontinued" (retired) before it gets boxed up for storage (archived) or thrown out (deleted). You don't skip straight to the dumpster from the sales floor.

questions.text:
A Configuration Manager wants to explore ServiceNow CMDB 360 saved queries to see if the reports can assist with managing of CMDB data.

What insights are gained from CMDB 360 queries? (Choose 2)

options.t: Unique CIs created from different data sources
Gaps in attribute data from different data sources
Different attribute values from different data sources
Orphan CIs created from different data sources
Duplicate configuration items from different data sources

questions.explanation: CMDB 360 (Multisource CMDB) is built to compare how different discovery sources see the same CI — surfacing gaps (missing attribute data from a source) and conflicts (different values reported for the same attribute). Duplicate and orphan CI detection are handled by identification rules and orphan rules feeding the Correctness KPI, not CMDB 360 queries specifically.
questions.analogy: Imagine three different witnesses describing the same car accident — CMDB 360 is the tool that lines up their statements side by side so you can see where they disagree (different values) or where one witness simply didn't mention a detail (a gap).

questions.text:
The CMDB Configuration Management team wants to manage de-duplication tasks generated from data ingested into the CMDB via the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE).

In which area of the CMDB Workspace can they locate these de-duplication tasks?

options.t: Total status tile under the My Work tab
CMDB feature adoption tile under the Insights tab
Important actions tile under the Home tab

questions.explanation: The Home tab's "Important actions" tile in CMDB Workspace is designed to surface time-sensitive housekeeping items — like de-duplication tasks generated when the IRE detects duplicate CIs — right where an admin lands when they open the workspace.
questions.analogy: It's the equivalent of a to-do widget on your phone's home screen, versus having to dig through a settings menu to find the same task.

questions.text:
An organization needs to maintain non-discoverable attributes, such as warranty expiration dates, for hardware CIs. These attributes are not updated by automated discovery tools.

What method ensures these attributes are accurately maintained for all CIs?

options.t: Use a scheduled data import to update the attributes from an external source
Create a new CI class specifically for non-discoverable attributes
Use the CMDB Reconciliation Engine to update the attributes

questions.explanation: Discovery and the IRE only populate attributes they can technically detect on a device. Warranty dates, contract terms, and similar business data live in external systems (like a vendor's warranty database), so a scheduled data import pulls that external data in on a regular cadence to keep it current.
questions.analogy: Discovery tools are like a technician who can scan a laptop's hardware specs, but has no way of knowing when the warranty expires — that information has to be imported from the vendor's own records on a schedule, like a monthly statement arriving in the mail.

questions.text:
A Manager needs information on how to correctly establish relationships between Infrastructure CIs, Technology Management Offerings (Technical Service Offerings), and Application Services within the CMDB.

Which CSDM domain would provide this information?
questions.explanation: Service Delivery / Manage Technical Services is the domain that models the "provider view" of deployed technology — Application Services, Technical Services, Technical Service Offerings, and the infrastructure that supports them. That's exactly the set of relationships described here.
questions.analogy: This is the domain that answers "what technical machinery is actually running, and what infrastructure keeps it alive?" — the engine room view, as opposed to the storefront (Sell/Consume) or the blueprint stage (Design).

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator seeks to understand the available tools for preventing, addressing, and remediating duplicate CIs.

Drag and drop each feature with the corresponding outcome. (Some options may not apply.)

pairs.desc: Can be assigned to groups for resolving duplicate CIs
Offers insight into duplicate CIs within the CMDB
Offers a solution to resolve de-duplication tasks in bulk
Provides a wizard to resolve de-duplication tasks individually

questions.explanation: These four tools work together across the duplicate-CI lifecycle: the Correctness scorecard first flags that duplicates exist; De-Duplication Tasks route the cleanup work to a responsible group; De-Duplication Templates let you resolve many similar duplicates at once (bulk); and the Duplicate CI Remediator wizard walks an admin through resolving one duplicate set carefully, attribute by attribute.
questions.analogy: Think of cleaning up a messy shared drive: the scorecard is the report showing how many duplicate files exist, the task is the ticket assigned to someone to fix it, the template is a "bulk rename/merge" macro, and the wizard is the careful one-by-one review for the trickier files.

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator uses the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard to gain insights into the CMDB. The results display low scores for several metrics.

Which actions can the CMDB Administrator take to improve the CMDB Health? (Choose 2)

options.t: Use the Remediation Playbooks linked beside each metric
Focus on metric(s) with Critical and High priorities
Adjust the metrics using exclusion rules to improve the scores

questions.explanation: The dashboard is designed to be actioned via its linked remediation playbooks, and best practice is to prioritize the metrics flagged Critical or High first, since those represent the biggest risk to data quality. Simply removing CIs or adjusting exclusion rules to make a score look better doesn't actually fix the underlying data problem — it just hides it.
questions.analogy: If your car's dashboard shows three warning lights, you read the manual for each light (playbook) and fix the most urgent one first (Critical/High priority) — you don't just tape over the warning lights to make the dashboard look calmer.

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator needs the fastest time to value solution for effectively ingesting, managing, and maintaining CIs and relationships.

Which management tool will accomplish this to import Windows computer data from SCCM?

options.t: Import set using JDBC data source connection to SCCM using transform maps
IntegrationHub ETL connection to SCCM using Robust Transform Engine (RTE)

questions.explanation: Service Graph Connectors are pre-built, ServiceNow-supported integrations designed for exactly this "fastest time to value" scenario — they come with out-of-the-box scheduled imports, mappings, and identification/reconciliation logic already wired up for SCCM, so you don't have to build transform maps or scripts from scratch.
questions.analogy: It's the difference between buying flat-pack furniture with pre-drilled holes and clear instructions (Service Graph Connector) versus cutting your own wood and figuring out the joinery yourself (custom import sets and transform maps).

questions.text:
An organization is updating the CMDB to include new asset types like IoT devices. Relevant CI classes need to be added and outdated ones need to be removed from the Principal Class filter to ensure accurate display in ITSM processes.

Which roles are needed to add or remove classes? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation: Changing which classes are marked as Principal Classes touches dictionary-level configuration, so it requires personalize_dictionary along with sn_cmdb_admin, the role that governs CMDB class administration. cmdb_query_builder only grants access to build CMDB queries, and sn_csdm_admin isn't the role tied to this specific action.
questions.analogy: It's like needing both a building permit (personalize_dictionary, for touching the underlying structure) and being the property owner of record (sn_cmdb_admin) before you can officially change what's listed on the building's directory board.

questions.text:
A Configuration Management team wants to confirm that all servers in the CMDB are correctly associated with their location.

Which CMDB Data Manager policy type does the team create?
questions.explanation: Certification policies validate that data meets defined standards on specific fields (for example, that the Location field is correctly populated) across a set of CIs. Attestation is closer to a human physically confirming a CI still exists, whereas Certification checks the correctness of specific field values.
questions.analogy: Certification is like a quality-control check confirming the label on a product matches what's actually inside the box, rather than confirming the box itself physically exists on the shelf (that's Attestation).

questions.text:
The Server [cmdb_ci_server] class uses a dynamic reconciliation rule of lowest value for the Disk Space (GB) field, while the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] class uses a dynamic reconciliation rule of most reported for the Disk Space (GB) field.

Given the following data sources that populate Windows Server data into the CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB:
Tivoli: 75 GB · ServiceNow: 75 GB · LANDesk: 50 GB · Attris: 80 GB

Which value would be added to the CMDB for the Disk Space (GB) field of a Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] record?
questions.explanation: Windows Server uses the "most reported" dynamic reconciliation rule, which picks the value that the largest number of data sources agree on, not the highest or lowest number. Here, 75 GB is reported by two sources (Tivoli and ServiceNow) while 50 GB and 80 GB are each reported by only one source, so 75 GB wins as the most commonly reported value.
questions.analogy: It's like taking a vote among four witnesses: two say "75," one says "50," one says "80." "Most reported" goes with whichever answer got the most votes — 75 — rather than the highest or lowest number called out.

questions.text:
An Asset Manager wants to ensure that Asset records and CI records are kept synchronized automatically.

How does the Manager do this? (Choose 2)

options.t: Ensure one-to-one physical mapping between Asset and CI
Ensure that the business rule to update Asset fields on change on the CI table is active
Ensure that scheduled jobs are run during off-business hours to ensure that sync happens
Ensure that the business rule to update CI fields on change on the asset table is active

questions.explanation: ServiceNow keeps Asset and CI records in sync through business rules that fire in both directions: one that pushes changes made on the CI table over to the linked Asset, and one that pushes changes made on the Asset table over to the linked CI. Both need to be active for two-way synchronization.
questions.analogy: It's like keeping two calendars in sync — you need automatic updates flowing both ways: changes on Calendar A show up on Calendar B, and changes on Calendar B show up on Calendar A. If only one direction is wired up, they'll drift apart.

questions.text:
User endpoint devices are imported into the CMDB and populate the 'Assigned to' [assigned_to] field on the Computer [cmdb_ci_computer] CI. The Asset team puts in a request for the Configuration Analysts to populate the 'Assigned to' field on the related Asset.

What action does a Configuration Analyst take to achieve this in an automated way?

options.t: Use the Asset-CI Field Mapping module to create a new rule to replicate the 'Assigned to' value between the asset and associated CI
Configure a business rule on the computer table to use a script to populate the 'Assigned to' field on the asset based on insert or update in the computer class 'Assigned to' field
Hide the 'Assigned to' field on the asset record and create a new field that dot walks to the related CI to get the 'Assigned to' value

questions.explanation: The Asset-CI Field Mapping module is the supported, out-of-the-box way to define which fields automatically replicate between a CI and its related Asset — no custom scripting required. Writing a custom business rule or hiding fields with dot-walking would both work technically, but they're unsupported customizations rather than the designed mechanism.
questions.analogy: It's the built-in "auto-fill" settings menu for linking two forms together, rather than writing your own macro to copy one field to another every time someone hits save.

questions.text:
A retail organization needs to ensure that incidents affecting customer-facing services are resolved quickly to reduce potential revenue loss.

Which CSDM attribute is used to prioritize these services?

options.t: Assignment Group on the CI record
Affected CIs in the Incident record
Service classification in the Technical Service
Business Criticality in the Service Offering

questions.explanation: Business Criticality on the Service Offering captures how important that specific offering is to the business (e.g., revenue impact), which is exactly the data ITSM processes use to prioritize incidents affecting customer-facing services — it directly ties technical impact to business consequence.
questions.analogy: It's the label on a hospital patient's chart that says how urgent their case is — everything downstream (which doctor gets called, how fast) is driven by that one criticality flag, not by which department the equipment happens to sit in.

questions.text:
The Change Management team in an organization wants to implement a Change across multiple CIs at the same time.

Which field on the Change Request form needs to be populated with a dynamic CI group?
questions.explanation: The Configuration Item field on a Change Request can be populated with a Dynamic CI Group, which represents a query-based set of CIs (for example, "all web servers in Detroit"). This lets a single Change record apply across many matching CIs at once instead of requiring one Change per CI.
questions.analogy: It's like addressing one memo to "all Sales staff" instead of writing a separate memo for every single person in the department — the dynamic CI group is that named distribution list.

questions.text:
A company wants to track regulatory compliance. ServiceNow has an artifact type called an information object as part of the CSDM framework.

What is the purpose of an information object?

options.t: It describes data in general on a group of Configuration Items.
It describes the logical data to the Business Applications.
It describes data exchanged between an API interface and an Application.

questions.explanation: An Information Object in the Design domain describes the logical data that a Business Application handles or exchanges — it's a conceptual data description tied to the application, useful for things like tracking regulated data types (e.g., PII) across the application landscape.
questions.analogy: If the Business Application is a filing cabinet, the Information Object is the label describing what kind of documents are stored inside it (e.g., "customer financial records") — it's about the nature of the data, not the wiring between systems.

questions.text: Where can an administrator perform Natural Language Queries (NLQ)?
questions.explanation: Natural Language Queries let a user type a plain-English question about CMDB data and get results, and this capability lives in CMDB Workspace, ServiceNow's unified place for exploring and managing CMDB data.
questions.analogy: It's like typing a question into a search bar instead of writing a database query — and that search bar lives inside the same workspace you already use to browse CMDB data.

questions.text:
The following identification rule for a CI class has been defined:

Hardware Rule — Identifier Entries Table:
• Serial Number — criterion attributes: serial_number, serial_number_type — priority 100
• Hardware — criterion attribute: serial_number — priority 200
• Hardware — criterion attribute: name — priority 300
• Network Adapter — criterion attributes: mac_address, name — priority 400

Two new CI records are imported into the hardware class of the CMDB:
CI1: The name of this CI record matches the name of an existing CI record in the CMDB.
CI2: The IP address of this CI record matches the IP address of an existing CI record in the CMDB.

Which is correct based on the identification rule and the imported CI records?

options.t: CI1 will be updated with matching record and CI2 will be inserted as new record.
CI1 and CI2 both will be inserted as new records.

questions.explanation: The IRE evaluates identifier entries in priority order (lowest number first) until it finds a match. CI1 matches on "name," which is a defined criterion attribute (priority 300), so it's recognized as the existing record and updated. CI2 only matches on IP address, which isn't listed as a criterion attribute in any identifier entry for this rule at all, so the IRE has no basis to treat it as an existing CI — it gets inserted as new.
questions.analogy: Think of airport check-in with a list of accepted ID types in priority order (passport, then driver's license, then loyalty card). CI1 shows an accepted ID (name) and gets matched to their existing reservation. CI2 shows something that's not on the accepted-ID list at all (IP address) — so the counter has no way to recognize them and issues a brand-new booking.

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator is working in the CI Class Manager on the Basic Info tab.

How can the class be set as a Principal Class?

options.t: Click the Principal Class UI Action button
Check the Principal Class check box
Select 'Yes' from the Principal Class choice list

questions.explanation: On the Basic Info tab of CI Class Manager, Principal Class is a simple checkbox — checking it flags that class as a Principal Class, which then makes it available in Principal Class filters used across ITSM processes.
questions.analogy: It's a plain on/off toggle, like ticking a checkbox to mark an email as "Important" — no separate button or dropdown menu needed.

questions.text:
A Configuration Manager is implementing end to end service modeling and wants to get help on status and playbooks for improving the quality.

What does the Configuration Manager reference to obtain guidance?
questions.explanation: The CSDM Data Foundation Dashboard specifically measures alignment to CSDM service-modeling guidance and links out to playbooks for improving that alignment — it's the CSDM-focused counterpart to the more general CMDB Health Dashboard.
questions.analogy: If the CMDB Health Dashboard checks "is your data clean?", the CSDM Data Foundation Dashboard checks "is your data modeled the way CSDM recommends?" — a different, more structural kind of health check.

questions.text:
The Incident Process Owner asks which classes of CSDM are used on the Incident form.

Which classes are appropriate? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation: CSDM guidance points Incident and other ITSM records at operational, discoverable classes — Service Offering and Application Service — because those represent live, running things that can actually be impacted. Business Application and Service Portfolio are more conceptual/planning-oriented classes (Design and Sell/Consume portfolio views) that aren't meant to be attached to operational incidents.
questions.analogy: An incident report references the actual running kitchen equipment that broke (Application Service) and the specific meal service affected (Service Offering) — not the restaurant's overall business plan (Business Application) or its menu strategy (Service Portfolio).

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator needs to configure a new application identification rule that considers the potential for the same application installed more than once on the same server.

Which is the best choice of a criterion attribute?
questions.explanation: When the same application can be installed multiple times on one server, the file path (the specific install directory) is what actually distinguishes each individual instance — file name, class, version, and port can all be identical across multiple installs of the same app, so they wouldn't reliably tell the installs apart.
questions.analogy: Imagine two identical apps installed in two different folders on the same computer. The file name and version are the same for both — the folder path is the one detail that actually tells them apart, like two identical twins living at two different addresses.

questions.text: Where can a CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB Saved Query be viewed and created in the CMDB Workspace?

options.t: Coverage window on the CMDB 360 tab
Saved queries window on the CMDB 360 tab
Saved queries window on the Insights tab

questions.explanation: Saved queries specific to CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB live in the Saved queries window under the CMDB 360 tab in CMDB Workspace — right alongside the multisource data they're built to query.
questions.analogy: It's like keeping your saved search filters in the same folder as the data set they search — not off in a completely different app.

questions.text:
A CMDB CI Class Owner responsible for the Windows Servers needs to manage the Windows Server class.

Which CI Class Manager feature will help the CI Class Owner streamline this task?
questions.explanation: Pinned Classes lets a CI Class Owner keep the classes they're responsible for (like Windows Server) readily accessible in CI Class Manager instead of searching for them every time.
questions.analogy: It's the same idea as pinning your most-used apps to your phone's home screen instead of scrolling through the full app list each time.

questions.text:
A Configuration Management Governance team is transitioning from utilizing legacy CMDB status fields to CSDM life cycle status fields.

Which table can be modified?
questions.explanation: The Life Cycle Mapping table is specifically where the correspondence between legacy status fields and the newer CSDM Life Cycle Stage/Stage Status values is configured and can be adjusted, which is why it's the table you'd touch during this kind of migration.
questions.analogy: It's the translation table between an old filing system's labels and a new one's labels — you edit the translation key itself, not the label sets on either side.

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator needs to prevent duplicate CI creation from import sets that load data into the CMDB from vendor shipment files containing CI information.

How can the Administrator do this?

options.t: Create comparison rules in the IRE
Use the CMDBTransformUtil API in the transform script
Set the system property to utilize the IRE within transform maps
Set the coalesce on two mappings within the transform map

questions.explanation: Setting coalesce on the appropriate field mappings in a transform map tells the import to check for an existing matching record (based on that field) before inserting — which is the standard mechanism to prevent duplicate records from a straightforward import set/transform map workflow.
questions.analogy: Coalesce fields work like a "check if this ID already exists before creating a new customer record" rule at checkout — match first, insert only if nothing matches.

questions.text:
The CMDB Health Dashboard is based on three Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): Correctness, Compliance, and Completeness. Each KPI includes several sub-metrics.

Drag the sub-metrics to the KPI. (Some options may not apply.)

pairs.desc: Required
Audit
Orphan

questions.explanation: Completeness aggregates Required and Recommended attribute checks. Compliance is driven by Audit results (desired-state comparisons). Correctness covers Orphan CIs, Staleness, and Duplicates. "Stability," "Certify," and "Suggested" aren't sub-metric names used by the dashboard.
questions.analogy: Think of a school report card: Completeness is "did you turn in all your assignments" (required work), Compliance is "did your answers meet the rubric" (audit against a standard), and Correctness is "is this still your current, undiscarded work" (not an orphaned or stale draft).

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator needs to set up CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB.

Drag and drop the system property to the functionality. (Some options may not apply.)

pairs.desc: glide.identification_engine.multisource_enabled

pairs.item: Enables capturing CMDB 360 data for CIs from non-CMDB classes
pairs.desc: glide.identification_engine.multisource_cmdb_ci_enabled
glide.cmdb.logger.source.cmdb_multisource

pairs.item: Maximum number of CIs that can be included in a CMDB 360 recompute operation
pairs.desc: glide.identification_engine.multisource.recompute.max.cii.limit

distractors: Enables capturing CMDB 360 data for CIs from CMDB classes
questions.explanation: Each of these system properties toggles a distinct, narrow piece of CMDB 360 functionality — the master on/off switch, an extension to non-CMDB classes, a logging toggle, and a numeric safety limit on how many CIs a recompute job will process at once (to protect performance).
questions.analogy: Think of a circuit breaker panel: one switch is the main power (multisource_enabled), one extends power to an outbuilding (non-CMDB classes), one just controls a warning light (logging), and one is a fuse limiting how much load can run at once (the recompute CI limit).

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator notices that CIs do not have a support group.

How can the support group be automatically populated and maintained on the CI record?

options.t: Technology Management Service Offering (Technical Service Offering)

questions.explanation: A Technical Service can be linked to a support group, and that relationship is used to automatically populate and keep the support group in sync on the CIs tied to that service — so the support team responsible for a given technical service is always identifiable from its CIs.
questions.analogy: It's like assigning a whole apartment building to one maintenance company — every unit in the building automatically inherits the same point of contact, rather than each tenant having to look one up individually.

questions.text: Where does a user with the appropriate role(s) review and manage the generated tasks after configuring CMDB Data Manager policies?

options.t: CMDB Health Dashboard > Duplicate CIs tab

questions.explanation: Once a Data Manager policy runs and generates tasks (like retire/archive/attestation tasks), the assigned users review and act on them from the My Work tab in CMDB Workspace, which centralizes tasks assigned to that person or group.
questions.analogy: It's your personal task inbox — the place you check to see what's been assigned to you, rather than a general dashboard report.

questions.text:
A global enterprise integrates data from multiple discovery sources such as ServiceNow Discovery, SCCM, AWS, and manual uploads to populate its CMDB. However, each discovery source categorizes the same CIs differently, leading to duplicate records and inconsistencies across the system. As a result, the CMDB team is struggling with data accuracy and standardization.

What actions does the CMDB team take to resolve the issue? (Choose 2)

options.t: Use CI Class Manager to establish standardized CI classes and attributes across all discovery sources
Allow each discovery source to define its own CI class, even if it results in inconsistencies
Implement and use identification and reconciliation rules to avoid duplicates and standardize CI classification
Create a custom script to manually adjust incoming data before storing it in the CMDB

questions.explanation: The supported approach is to standardize on shared CI classes/attributes via CI Class Manager and let the Identification and Reconciliation Engine handle matching and resolving conflicting data from multiple sources — that's precisely what IRE is built for. Letting each source define its own classes (B) recreates the original problem, and custom scripting (D) works around the platform instead of using its built-in tools.
questions.analogy: It's like getting every department in a company to agree on one shared naming convention and filing system (standardized classes), then using a receptionist whose job is to recognize "Bob from Sales" and "Robert Smith, Sales Dept" as the same person (IRE) — rather than letting every department invent its own naming scheme.

questions.text:
A Configuration Manager working in the CMDB Workspace wants to see how CIs are connected to each other.

Which tool can be used?
questions.explanation: The Relationship Map visualizes direct connections between CIs — a straightforward graph of what's linked to what — which is the tool for the general "how are CIs connected" question. The Unified Map is more oriented toward viewing a service's full topology with contextual detail, and "Business Service Map" isn't the specific tool name here.
questions.analogy: The Relationship Map is like a simple wiring diagram showing which devices plug into which — quick and direct, versus a full architectural blueprint (Unified Map) that layers in more contextual information.

questions.text:
A CMDB team has noticed that some hardware CIs are missing the serial number information, making it difficult to maintain data accuracy. The team needs a structured approach to identify and address these gaps.

Which accomplishes this task?
questions.explanation: A CMDB Data Foundation Playbook is a step-by-step guide tied to a specific data-quality metric (like missing serial numbers) that walks the team through diagnosing and fixing the root cause — exactly the "structured approach" being described.
questions.analogy: It's the recipe card that comes with a specific dashboard warning — not the whole kitchen (CI Class Manager) or a new ingredient delivery service (Service Graph Connectors), but the actual instructions for fixing this one problem.

questions.text:
A ServiceNow Administrator wants to implement Service Graph Connectors to provide integrations to many third-party solutions that the company wants integrated into the CMDB.

Which categories of connectors are available to the Administrator? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation: Service Graph Connectors are organized by category on the ServiceNow Store, with Cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.) and Observability (monitoring/APM tools) among the recognized categories. "Workflow Automation" and "DevOps" aren't the category labels used for this connector catalog.
questions.analogy: Think of an app store organized into sections like "Cloud Tools" and "Monitoring Tools" — you're picking from the actual section headings the store uses, not inventing your own category names.

questions.text:
Using CI Class Manager, the Tomcat identification rule has the following criterion attributes configured: Class, Install Directory.

Which identifier entry configuration option must be checked to attempt a match using the Application identification rule if no match is found using the Tomcat identification rule?
questions.explanation: "Allow fallback to parent's rules" tells the IRE that if the Tomcat class's own identification rule doesn't find a match, it should try the identification rule of the parent class (Application) as a backup, rather than giving up or creating a duplicate.
questions.analogy: It's like a customer service rep who checks a specialist policy first, and if that doesn't apply, is explicitly allowed to fall back to the general company policy instead of leaving the case unresolved.

questions.text: Drag and drop the product to its description.

pairs.desc: Automatically identifies devices and applications in the network, populating the CMDB with accurate and up-to-date information
Facilitates integration between ServiceNow and external systems to import and synchronize data
Complete topology of the services and shows how they are supported by underlying infrastructure and applications
Provides real-time visibility into endpoint configurations, populating the CMDB with accurate and up-to-date information

questions.explanation: Each tool covers a different ingestion approach: Discovery actively scans the network agentlessly; Service Graph Connectors pull data from external/third-party systems via APIs; Service Mapping builds full application-to-infrastructure topologies; and ACC is an installed agent that reports endpoint data in near real time.
questions.analogy: Discovery is like a patrol car driving the neighborhood checking on houses; Service Graph Connectors are like a mail-forwarding service from other post offices; Service Mapping draws the full delivery route showing how packages flow through the whole system; and ACC is like a resident reporting live updates about their own house.

questions.text:
A Configuration Management team needs to prevent duplicate server records to avoid confusion among users. Server records are identified when they are processed via the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) using the configured identification rules.

Where would these rules be configured?
questions.explanation: Identification rules (and their identifier entries/criterion attributes) are configured per CI class in CI Class Manager, which is the tool built specifically for managing class-level structure and rules like this.
questions.analogy: It's the settings page for a specific product line, not a general dashboard — you go to where the class itself is defined to change how it's identified.

questions.text:
The CMDB Administrator has been asked to establish Configuration Management with a functional CMDB.

Which factor is most critical for successfully operationalizing the CMDB in ServiceNow?

options.t: Establishing clear governance and continuously monitoring CMDB health
Relying on automated discovery tools to maintain and update CMDB records
Populating the CMDB with as much data as possible to ensure a comprehensive inventory of CIs
Allowing IT teams to modify CMDB records as needed to promote flexibility in data management

questions.explanation: ServiceNow's own CMDB best-practice guidance stresses that a CMDB is an ongoing program, not a one-time project — it needs clear governance (owners, processes) and continuous health monitoring to stay trustworthy over time. Automation alone, sheer data volume, or unrestricted edit access don't guarantee accuracy or long-term reliability without that governance layer.
questions.analogy: A CMDB is more like a community garden than a one-time planting: without ongoing tending and clear rules about who's responsible for which bed, it doesn't matter how much you planted on day one — it goes to weeds.

questions.text:
A Configuration Management Process Owner needs to configure Data Manager for policy tasks to be correctly assigned and aligned with the group attribute assigned to a class in CI Class Manager.

Which is the recommended field to be used for policy task assignment?
questions.explanation: "Managed by group" is the attribute configured at the class level in CI Class Manager to designate ownership responsibility, so Data Manager policies use this same field to route generated tasks to the right group consistently.
questions.analogy: It's like routing all maintenance tickets to whichever team is listed as the building's official property manager — you use the one authoritative ownership field, not a different list each time.

questions.text:
A CMDB CI Class Owner has been asked to change the icon for the UNIX Server class.

Which CI Class Manager tab can the owner use to change the icon for the class?
questions.explanation: Basic Info is where high-level, identity-related class settings live — name, description, icon, and the Principal Class checkbox — so that's where you'd go to change something visual like the class icon.
questions.analogy: It's the "profile settings" page for the class — the place you'd update a display photo, not the detailed settings pages further in.

questions.text:
An organization is using CMDB Query Builder to find all application services with a database that has incidents and all infrastructure in those application services.

Which steps does the organization take to build this query? (Choose 2)

options.t: Add a non-CMDB table to the query
Use a Service Mapping Query to include non-CMDB tables like the Incident table
Use a Service Mapping Query to find all incidents related to the database
Use a CMDB Query to include application services and their related infrastructure

questions.explanation: CMDB Query Builder offers two complementary query types for this scenario: a Service Mapping Query, which can reach beyond pure CMDB tables to pull in related non-CMDB records like Incidents, and a CMDB Query, which traverses CI relationships to gather application services and their supporting infrastructure. Combining both gets you the full picture the scenario asks for.
questions.analogy: It's like using two different search tools for one investigation — one tool that pulls in related case files from outside the main filing system (Incidents), and another that maps out everyone connected in the org chart (application services and infrastructure) — then combining both results.

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator has installed a Service Graph Connector (SGC), and then made customizations to the mappings.

Which is a consequence of this action?

options.t: The customized mappings are not supported by ServiceNow, and the customer is responsible for supporting their own customized SGC.
The customization will prevent the SGC from executing without an approval record attached to the affected mapping record.
Fields populated by a customization will have a special tag associated with them in the CMDB.

questions.explanation: ServiceNow provides Service Graph Connectors as pre-built, supported integrations, but once an admin customizes the out-of-the-box mappings, that customization falls outside ServiceNow's support scope — the organization becomes responsible for maintaining and supporting their own modified version going forward.
questions.analogy: It's like a manufacturer's warranty on a car: it covers the factory-built parts, but once you swap in your own custom modifications, you're on your own for supporting those changes.

questions.text: Which ServiceNow solutions automatically create relationships between CI Applications that are part of an Application Service? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation: Service Mapping and Discovery are the tools designed to actually trace real connections between running application components and automatically build the relationship records that tie them into an Application Service. IntegrationHub ETL, Data Manager, and Event Management serve different purposes (data transformation, lifecycle policies, and event correlation, respectively) and aren't built to auto-discover CI relationships.
questions.analogy: Discovery and Service Mapping are like technicians who physically trace the cables between servers and note down what's connected to what — the other tools listed do different jobs entirely (moving data, managing lifecycle, watching for alerts), not cable-tracing.

questions.text:
A Configuration Manager responsible for a specific region wants to use the CMDB Health Dashboard to improve the data quality of the CMDB for that region. The Configuration Manager only sees the overall score and grouped by CI Class.

How can the Configuration Manager get a score for regionally relevant CIs?

options.t: Create CMDB groups with type, health, by region
Customize the CMDB Health Dashboard scheduled jobs to group the results by region
On the CMDB health settings, activate the option, Group scores by region

questions.explanation: CMDB Groups (a Foundation domain concept) let you define a custom grouping of CIs based on chosen criteria — such as region — and the Health Dashboard can then report scores against that group. There's no built-in "group by region" toggle on the scheduled jobs or health settings; you create the grouping yourself via CMDB Groups.
questions.analogy: It's like creating a custom playlist (the CMDB Group) so your music app can show you stats just for that playlist, instead of hoping the app has a built-in "by mood" filter already baked in.

questions.text:
The CMDB Administrator group seeks to filter specific CI classes that display on the CMDB Health Dashboard. This ensures that only relevant data is displayed, excluding items that are not ready for management.

Which feature can the group utilize to achieve this goal?
questions.explanation: Health Inclusion Rules control which CIs are counted as part of CMDB Health calculations — by default all CIs are included, but inclusion rules let you filter out classes or records not yet ready to be measured, so the dashboard reflects genuinely relevant data.
questions.analogy: It's like setting up filters on a survey so responses from a test group don't skew your real results — you're deciding who's actually eligible to be counted.

questions.text:
ServiceNow provides a suite of CMDB management tools designed to effectively ingest, manage, and maintain CIs and relationships.

Drag and drop the design architecture to its management tool. (Some options may not apply.)

pairs.desc: Automated agent-based solution running patterns
Organization-built solution using transform maps
Third-party integrations from other vendors
Automated agentless solution running patterns

distractors: Pre-built store integration solutions that require minimal customization
questions.explanation: Each tool has a distinct architecture: ACC installs an agent on the endpoint that reports data automatically; Import Sets are what your own team builds and maintains using transform maps; Service Graph Connectors are integrations built by third-party vendors/partners; and Discovery is agentless — it scans devices remotely without installing software on them.
questions.analogy: ACC is like a resident who lives in the house and reports on it directly (agent-based); Discovery is like a drone flying overhead scanning houses without ever going inside (agentless); Import Sets are the spreadsheet your own team built and maintains; and a Service Graph Connector is a pre-wired connection built by an outside vendor.

questions.text: Which shows the most complete list of policy types that are provided by the CMDB Data Manager?

options.t: Retire, Archive, Attestation, Certification, and Delete

questions.explanation: CMDB Data Manager's full set of policy types is Retire, Archive, Delete, Attestation, and Certification — the other answer options are all missing at least one of these five.
questions.analogy: It's a checklist of five distinct tools in the toolbox; any answer missing one of them is just an incomplete inventory.

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator wants to leverage dynamic reconciliation rules.

Which feature must be enabled?
questions.explanation: Dynamic reconciliation rules (like "most reported" or "lowest value") depend on having multiple sources reporting on the same CI, which is exactly what CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB tracks and enables — it's the underlying feature that makes dynamic rules possible in the first place.
questions.analogy: Dynamic reconciliation rules are like a vote-counting mechanism — but you need the voter registration system (CMDB 360/Multisource) turned on first, or there's no pool of votes to count from.

questions.text: How is the CMDB aligned to business processes? (Choose 2)

options.t: Extends service delivery management to all enterprise departments
Enhances decision-making and operational efficiency across the organization
Enables the CFO/CIO to track software licenses
Provides a centralized view of configuration items and their relationships

questions.explanation: The CMDB's core value proposition is being a single, centralized, relationship-aware view of the IT estate, which in turn supports better organization-wide decision-making and operational efficiency. The other two options describe narrower, specific use cases (a particular license-tracking function, or a sweeping claim about extending to "all enterprise departments") rather than the CMDB's general alignment to business processes.
questions.analogy: It's the difference between describing what a company's shared database is fundamentally for (a single source of truth that helps everyone make better decisions) versus naming one narrow report that a specific executive might pull from it.

questions.text:
A Configuration Manager needs to ingest third-party CIs into the CMDB.

Which method minimizes the risk of technical debt?
questions.explanation: Service Graph Connectors are built and maintained by ServiceNow (or certified partners) with ongoing updates, so they minimize the custom code and manual upkeep your team would otherwise be on the hook for — that upkeep burden is exactly what "technical debt" refers to here. Building your own solution via Table API or transform maps means your team owns all future maintenance.
questions.analogy: Buying a professionally maintained appliance with a service plan (Service Graph Connector) versus building your own custom machine from scratch (Table API/transform maps) that only you know how to repair when it breaks.

questions.text: What is the relationship between an application and a server?
questions.explanation: The out-of-the-box CMDB relationship type here reads as Application "Runs" on Server, with the reverse direction being Server "Runs On" back to the Application — captured as the paired relationship type Runs::Runs On.
questions.analogy: It's like a job title pair: from the Application's side you'd say "I run on that server," and from the Server's side you'd say "that application runs on me" — same relationship, described from each direction.

questions.text: How does a CMDB Administrator use the ServiceNow Platform to ensure the data quality associated with CIs in the CMDB?
questions.explanation: Data Quality checks run through scheduled jobs that periodically evaluate CI data against configured rules — a recurring, automated check rather than something triggered ad hoc by a business rule on save.
questions.analogy: It's a routine inspection that runs on a schedule (like a nightly security sweep), not a rule that only fires the instant someone edits a specific record.

questions.text:
The ITSM Manager wants to use Technology Management Offerings (Technical Service Offerings) to populate the support group of associated CIs.

What CSDM stage would this be completed in?
questions.explanation: CSDM's phased adoption model runs Foundation → Crawl → Walk → Run → Fly. Using Technical Service Offerings to actively drive operational data like support group assignment reflects a more mature stage of adoption — the Run phase, where the focus shifts to understanding technology's impact on business operations, not just establishing the basic building blocks (Crawl/Walk).
questions.analogy: Crawl and Walk are like learning to set up your filing cabinets and label folders; Run is like actually using that filing system to automatically route incoming mail to the right department — a more advanced, operational use of the same structure.

questions.text:
A Configuration Manager is reviewing the life cycle of CIs to ensure data accuracy, consistency, and relevance. The manager reviews the legacy status values and their equivalent CSDM life cycle stage and life cycle stage status values.

Where are these reviewed?
questions.explanation: Life cycle mappings are exactly where the correspondence between older/legacy status values and the newer CSDM Life Cycle Stage and Life Cycle Stage Status values is defined and reviewed.
questions.analogy: Same idea as an earlier question: it's the translation key connecting an old labeling system to a new one, and that's the specific place you'd go to review or adjust it.

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator is using the Duplicate CI Remediator to address a de-duplication task. On the first tab of the wizard, the Main CI is selected.

Which attributes are used to identify the Main CI? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation: The Duplicate CI Remediator suggests which duplicate should become the "Main" surviving CI based on signals like which record is the oldest (most established, likely most referenced historically) and which has the most related items (most connected, so keeping it preserves the most existing relationships).
questions.analogy: When merging two duplicate contact entries in your phone, you'd naturally keep the older, more established entry with the most linked history (call logs, messages) rather than the newer, more isolated one — same logic here.

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator wants to use the CMDB and CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard.

Where can the Administrator obtain the dashboard?

options.t: It is a free application on the ServiceNow Innovation Lab.
It is a paid application on the ServiceNow Store.
It is a free application on the ServiceNow Store.

questions.explanation: The CMDB and CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard is available as a free plugin/application on the ServiceNow Store — it needs to be actively installed, it isn't active out of the box by default, and it isn't a paid product or something sourced from an "Innovation Lab."
questions.analogy: Think of it like a free add-on you have to go download from an app store — it doesn't come pre-installed on the device, and there's no charge to get it.

questions.text:
A Platform Owner is building the governance team to support the CSDM.

Drag the domain to the roles that make up the governance team.

pairs.desc: Service Owner(s), Platform Owner
Technology Service Owner(s), Application Service Owner(s), Platform Owner
Enterprise Architect(s), Platform Owner
Enterprise Architect(s), Data Steward(s), Process Owner(s), Platform Owner

questions.explanation: CSDM governance assigns different personas to different domains based on who actually owns the decisions in that area: Service Owners anchor the Foundation, Technology/Application Service Owners anchor Portfolio-related tables, Enterprise Architects lead Design decisions, and the Technical Domain draws on a broader mix (Architects, Data Stewards, Process Owners) because it spans both design and operational concerns — with the Platform Owner involved across all of them as the connective role.
questions.analogy: It's like a company's org chart for a big cross-functional project: different specialists own different sections, but there's always one program manager (the Platform Owner) with a seat at every table to keep everything connected.

questions.text:
An Enterprise Architect needs to help the CMDB owner understand the benefits of CSDM.

Drag the CSDM domains to the respective benefits.

pairs.desc: Understand CIs related to business application and related capabilities, identify redundancies, monitor costs and make better investment decisions around roadmap
Understand technical services, technical service offerings, service support and all relationships to underlying technology CIs
Understand business services and ownership, cost, scope of what's offered to the business/consumer and request access to the business service
Use the base system tables when implementing the CSDM to derive the highest value from ServiceNow products and the Now Platform

questions.explanation: Each domain delivers a distinct kind of business value: Design & Planning gives visibility into applications/capabilities for roadmap and cost decisions; Service Delivery gives operational visibility into how technical services are supported; Service Consumption gives the business-facing view of what's offered and to whom; and Foundation is the underlying data layer that makes every other domain, and every ServiceNow product built on top of it, work correctly.
questions.analogy: Think of a company built in layers: Foundation is the building's structural framework everything else stands on; Design & Planning is the architect's blueprint for future renovations; Service Delivery is the facilities team keeping the building running; and Service Consumption is the tenant directory showing who's renting what space.

questions.text:
A CMDB Administrator, viewing the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard, notices the Unique Locations Result percentage low.

What is the recommended process from the associated playbook to correct this issue?

options.t: Retain the location that matches the organization's standard naming convention, and delete the duplicate without further validation
Keep both locations as either can be used as a valid alternate location
Review both locations, update CIs with the correct location and delete the duplicate location
Use the Duplicate CI Remediator to merge the duplicate location records

questions.explanation: The recommended playbook approach is a careful, verified cleanup: review both duplicate location records, reassign the CIs pointing to the wrong one over to the correct location, and only then remove the duplicate — protecting against silently breaking references by skipping validation.
questions.analogy: It's like consolidating two duplicate customer addresses in a database: you check which one is actually correct, make sure every order record points to the right address, and only then delete the leftover duplicate — you don't just delete first and hope nothing important was pointing at it.

questions.text:
A CMDB Manager wants to start adding CSDM design and planning (design) domain components into the CMDB.

Who is involved in this exercise? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation: The Design & Planning domain (Business Capabilities, Business Applications, Information Objects) is primarily the territory of the Application Owner, who owns the application itself, and the Enterprise Architect, who designs how capabilities and applications map to business goals. Application Service Owner and Business Relationship Manager are personas tied to other domains (Service Delivery and Sell/Consume, respectively).
questions.analogy: Designing the blueprint of a building involves the architect and the person who owns the building's intended use — not the facilities manager who runs it day to day, or the leasing agent who sells space in it. Those are important roles, just for a different stage.
